title: OKTAVIAN aluminium sphere, leakage neutron and photon spectra (D-T point source)

source.original_experiment: Osaka University OKTAVIAN fusion neutronics benchmark (via the IAEA-NDS repository, partly adopted from CoNDERC); the original publication was not read in this pass

license.attribution: Experimental spectra and input files from IAEA-NDS/open-benchmarks (IAEA Nuclear Data Section), CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/, commit 1d9855b00e05c5d5e25a11026ac56940dc75b516; partly adopted from the IAEA CoNDERC compilation. The tables in this manifest were copied unchanged from the experimental CSV files named under files; no other change was made.
license.terms: Upstream states that all contents, including input files, reference output and experimental data, are CC-BY-4.0.

files.role: openmc materials (as published; see not_covered and the runner for the material defect)
mcnp input (source spectrum, tallies, full material compositions)
experimental neutron spectrum, coarse bins (derived sums, not scored)
experimental photon spectrum, coarse bins (derived sums, not scored)

normalisation.quantity: leakage spectrum from the sphere surface at r = 19.95 cm
normalisation.units: neutrons per source neutron per unit lethargy; photons per source neutron per MeV
normalisation.source_normalisation: per source neutron (D-T source, MCNP sdef histogram si1/sp1 in the MCNP input)
normalisation.location: spherical surface 6 (r = 19.95 cm) of the MCNP model; the experiment is a time-of-flight detector at about 11 m
normalisation.reaction_or_particle: neutrons above 100 keV; photons 0.5 to 11 MeV
normalisation.energy_integration: neutron: log-spaced bins of constant lethargy width (about 0.04); photon: 0.1 MeV bins to 5 MeV, then 0.5 MeV bins
normalisation.basis: Inferred from numbers, not documented upstream. The packaged openmc_fusion_benchmarks experiment.h5 holds per-cm2 surface values; the CSV values equal those times 4*pi*19.5^2 = 4778.36 cm2 divided by the lethargy width (neutrons, constant ratio 1.1946e5 = 4778.36/0.04, scatter 0.05 %) or the bin width in MeV (photons, ratio constant to 1e-11 within each width). The area uses r = 19.5 cm although the tally surface is at 19.95 cm.
normalisation.why: the unit is inferred from a numeric identity with a second packaging, the upstream tally is a flux (MCNP F2) not a current, and the area radius differs from the tally surface
normalisation.next_step: confirm against the CoNDERC record or the original publication, then set status to confirmed

components.name: Error column as provided
components.meaning: absolute 1 sigma assumed, same units as Value; upstream does not state whether it is statistical only or includes systematic terms or a normalisation uncertainty

uncertainty.note: Relative values run from about 0.2 % near the 15 MeV peak to above 80 % in the last bins; a statistical-only column would make the test stricter than the experiment justifies.

compatibility.k_basis: authored: coverage factor 2 on the combined standard uncertainty, assuming the Error column is a 1 sigma value (unconfirmed)

covariance.basis: authored: the calculation shares no random input or measurement with the experiment, so Cov(C, E) = 0; shared source or normalisation terms are inside u_E as published or not stated

neutron_leakage_spectrum.unit: n per source neutron per unit lethargy
neutron_leakage_spectrum.description: neutron leakage, 134 bins from 97 keV to 20.66 MeV

photon_leakage_spectrum.unit: photons per source neutron per MeV

bin.edge_convention: CSV energy is the upper edge of the e21 tally bin (identical edge list in the MCNP input)

blocked.why: the first bin (97.1 to 101.1 keV) straddles the 100 keV lower limit of the time-of-flight measurement
blocked.next_step: score only bins entirely above 100 keV, or confirm the measurement range in the original publication

qualified_range.geometry_class: spherical shell assembly, 19.95 cm outer radius, one beam-tube cylinder
qualified_range.spectrum_class: D-T point source with the MCNP histogram energy distribution, leakage observed above 100 keV

known_upstream_defects: The published OpenMC materials.xml gives the steel shells as pure Cr50 (weight fraction 1.0, 7.824 g/cm3) and aluminium as pure Al27, while the MCNP input gives 13-nuclide stainless steel and aluminium with Si, Fe and Cu impurities. The OpenMC file also has no settings, source or tallies. The FARIS runner builds materials from the MCNP input and keeps the OpenMC geometry; it does not use the published OpenMC materials.
The MCNP photon tally f41:p names cell 6, which has zero importance.
